title: Array Indexing
prompt:
Access and manipulate elements of an array using indexing
Sample Input: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
Sample Output: 1, 5
answer:
Sure, I'd be happy to help you with that! In many programming languages, you can access and manipulate elements of an array (or a list) using indexing. Here's how you can do it in JavaScript:

Suppose you have an array named `numbers` that contains the elements you provided in the sample input:

```javascript
const numbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
```

To access the first element (index 0) of the array, you can use the square bracket notation like this:

```javascript
console.log(numbers[0]); // Output: 1
```

To access the last element (index 4) of the array, you can use the same notation:

```javascript
console.log(numbers[4]); // Output: 5
```

If you want to modify the value of an element in the array, you can assign a new value to the corresponding index. For example:

```javascript
numbers[1] = 10; // Replace the second element with 10
console.log(numbers); // Output: [1, 10, 3, 4, 5]
```

I hope this helps! Let me know if you have any other questions.
